Violation ID: 973242
Permit API: 059-23556
Unconventional: No
County: Greene
Municipality: Cumberland Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/21/2022
Comments: On 10/21/22 a routine complete inspection of the McClure 3 OG well site was conducted.During the inspection, the following was observed:-A well tag was present on the wellhead (Photo #1).-Well and operator information was visible at the well site (Photo #2).-Some corrosion was noted on the well and production equipment (Photos #3 and #12).-Severe corrosion and holes were present in the production tank (Photos #4-5).-Saturated substrate that exhibited elevated conductivity was observed outside of the production tank inside the earthen containment berm (Photos #4-9). -Deer tracks were prevalent throughout the saturated area. -The fluid remaining inside the tank exhibited conductivity above the maximum level of detection for my probe (20mS) (Photo #8).-The deer tracks and elevated conductivity were observed in front of the earthen berm as well (Photos #10-11). I contacted Brian Goletz of Diversified to inform him of the release. He stated that the tank is scheduled to be replaced. According to Mr. Goletz, the new tank has been acquired and is scheduled to be replaced likely within a week. Violations of 78.57(a), 78.54, and 91.34 are being issued for the brine release.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 1/04/2024 to PIN OAK ENERGY PARTNERS LLC in Mercer Borough, Mercer county. OGA3220(A) - PLUGGING REQUIREMENTS - Failure to plug the well upon abandoning it.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PIN OAK ENERGY PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/04/2024
Violation Code: OGA3220(A) - PLUGGING REQUIREMENTS - Failure to plug the well upon abandoning it.
Violation ID: 8170318
Permit API: 085-23446
Unconventional: No
County: Mercer
Municipality: Mercer Borough
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/04/2024
Comments: Routine follow up field inspection performed in the afternoon with cold, partly cloudy weather conditions and 33 degrees. Last inspection (#3654443) performed on 12/5/2023, nearly one month ago. Inspection #3654443 / Isoldi Unit 1 085-23446 Notice of Violation (NOV) mailed to Operator (Pin Oak) by the Department on 12/11/2023 as Certified Mail No. 9589 0710 5270 0566 5253 96. Violations included OGA3211(G) and OGA3220(A). Refer to (photos #1 and #2) for screen capture images of NOV cover letter mailing. Correspondence from the Operator (Pin Oak) as response letter, dated 12/19/2023 and received by the Department on 12/28/2023. Refer to (photo #3) for screen capture image of Operator response letter. Operator states in response letter that proper signage/posting has been affixed to surface facility tank, which addresses NOV OGA3211(G). The Operator states in response letter that well has been recently acquired and production is being evaluated currently. The Operator also states that they will make a recommendation by 6/1/2024 regarding production reestablishment or well plugging. At the wellhead, no changes to configuration since prior inspection (photos #4 and #5). Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead (photo #6). Meter reading (photo #7). Some fair corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. The surface/ground production facility and one 100 bbl steel tank all contained by an earthen dike (photo #8). Valve cracked open on main tubular feeding facility/separator with open valves to and from separator (photo #9). A new 31-day production chart is present with no distinct markings and dated 1/1/24 (photo #10). A pipeline, MRM 3200 is located adjacent, just North of surface production facility. The new well posting signage is affixed to steel tank with all information readable about well and current Operator present. The new well posting affixed on steel tank adheres to Departments request and complies with OGA3211(G) (photo #11). Trace to occasionally fair corrosion on ground production unit equipment and tank. Closed Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The Operator submitted 2022 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well stating 355 psig. The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2022 is blank indicating this well was not in production during the 2022 production year. Additionally, this well noted as having blank production under the gas and/or oil quantity columns and noted as Well Temporarily Not Producing under the non production comments columns of the '22, '21, '20, and '19 annual production reports. The last reported production was in 2018 with 568 Mcf recorded over 365 days. During prior inspection on 12/5/23, the OGI spoke to the land/home owner who stated that house gas is not being provided currently and has not been provided in many years. Given this information, the prior inspection, and todays inspection the well remains abandoned and has not been operational in over 4 years. Continued Notice of violation (NOV) issued for well abandonment OGA3220(A). This is not an active, producing well. The well is abandoned and continues to be temporarily shut in while the Operator evaluates the well. No new production recorded since prior inspection on 12/5/23.

Permit API: 031-23676
Unconventional: No
County: Clarion
Municipality: Monroe Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/26/2026
Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow up to Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection inspection #4020256 conducted on July 24, 2025 at 0907 hrs. During the inspection, the wellhead and casing strings were visually assessed for signs of leakage, structural deterioration, and or failure. While on-site the well was shut in and not producing. The 7" intermediate casing was being vented to atmosphere through the annulus vent valve at a concentration of 97% combustible gas. The landowner is no longer receiving gas from this well. To evaluate the potential for subsurface gas migration, four slam bar holes were installed approximately 6 inches to 1 foot from the well-bore in the cardinal directions. Each hole was placed to a depth of approximately 3 feet. Soil gas measurements were obtained using a Bascom-Turner Gas Explorer II meter, calibrated on March 26, 2026. All slam bar holes at the time of inspection were non-detect for combustible gas. As of the completion of this inspection, the operator has not plugged the well nor remedied any of the outstanding violations associated with the well. A previous check valve violation created in error has been closed.

properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 3/10/2026 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in German Township, Fayette county. OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 3/10/2026
Violation Code: OGA3211(H) - WELL PERMITS - LABELING - Failure to install, in a permanent manner, the permit number on a completed well.
Violation ID: 8267340
Permit API: 051-21425
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: German Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/10/2026
Comments: On March 10 2026, the Department conducted a routine inspection of the CFR/USX 5 OG Well in regards to OGI referral.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department traveled down the access road towards the well site. Approximately halfway down the access road, the Department observed water flowing onto the access road. The water was observed continuing to flow down the access road where it appeared to end at the well site. Erosion channels appear to have formed along the access road as a result of the flowing water.Upon further inspection, the water appears to be originating from a drainage channel/tributary to Antram Run. It appears that a culvert located under the access road may be damaged or obstructed, causing the water to flow onto the access road rather than through the culvert. The Department was unable to locate/inspect the culvert inlet. However, no water was observed discharging from the culvert outlet. Based on these observations, it appears the water is flowing from the drainage channel/trib to Antram Run onto the access road rather than through the culvert.Upon further inspection of the well site, the well appeared equipped for production. A well tag was present on the well head, however had a previous operator listed (Apex Energy). No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface of the wellhead.A well posting was observed on a piece of production equipment and appeared to have all required information. However, it appeared damage and almost falling off. A production tank was observed onsite and appeared in sound condition. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the surface around the production tank.Prior to leaving the site the Department spoke with operator representative Heather Empfield and informed her of the E and S issues related to the access road caused by the flowing water as well as recommended a new well tag/well posting be installed at the well site.Ms. Empfield stated that she would contact the site foreman to inform them of the Department's observations and they would work to assess the site and correct any issues as necessary.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed erosion of the access road, failure to maintain the culvert, as well as failure to have the well properly posted.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/03/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/03/2026
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 8284096
Permit API: 123-49194
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/03/2026
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted to document a field review of the recent removal of grub material previously located between the proposed Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads. William Cenk and Brian Bennett of Trinity Mineral Partners (TMP) were present for the duration of this inspection. Brian Ayers (WQSS) and I, Mathew Haemer (WQS), were present to represent the Department.During the 07/21/26 JPA pre-application meeting between TMP and the Department, Department Technical Services staff requested that the grub material placed south of the roadway between the Akins #3 and Akins #4 well pads be removed as soon as possible to potentially restore the hydrology near the road and well pad construction back to its original condition. It was observed that the grub material had impeded and redirected the flow of an Unnamed Tributary to Jackson Run and had begun to cause E and S problems alongside the roadway, well pad, and below the well pad for the proposed Akins #4 conventional well.At the time of this inspection, it appeared that all of the grub material had been removed as requested. However, TMP had also elected to redefine one of the stream channels below the well pad for Akins #3 and direct its flow through the disturbed area south of the roadway to Akins #4. The excavation work related to this stream channel continues to cause erosion and sedimentation to occur alongside the roadway and well pad for the proposed Akins #4. This is not the outcome Technical Services staff intended to result from the removal of the grub material. At the time of this inspection, the newly excavated stream channel is unprotected from erosion. There are three filter socks installed south of the Akins #4 well pad beyond the excavated stream channel directly in line with this channelized flow. Filter sock is not designed to be installed in channelized flow. All three filter socks are being undercut by the channelized flow. Evidence of erosion and sedimentation is still present before and after each filter sock. The area south and continuing west of Akins #4 that is now accepting the flow of this stream water is beginning to erode. A forested wetland is located west and down grade from the Akins #4 well pad. Bank erosion and saturated earth below the wetland indicate that the stream water overflows the wetland during storm events.The Department has yet to receive an updated E and S Plan that meets the expectations of the Technical Services staff. It is recommended that no further earth disturbance occurs without notification to and approval by the Department.The encroachment violations and violations relating to erosion and sediment control continue in the present condition of this construction and related excavation work.The violation for failure to post the well permit during construction has been closed.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/25/2024
Violation Code: CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8184833
Permit API: 125-28816
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Cecil Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/25/2024
Comments: On April 25, 2024 the Department conducted an inspection of the Augustine George 11039 access road located in Cecil Township, Washington County in regards to a complaint received on 04/24/24 CTS # 380091. The findings are as follows: At the time of the inspection, a truck was observed opening a valve and releasing what appeared to be freshwater onto the access road. Upon investigating this release, John Hulsey of Range Resources informed the Department that this fluid is freshwater and that the purpose of releasing said freshwater is to minimize the amount of dust caused from vehicles traveling up and down the access road. The released freshwater mixed with sediment as it flowed down the access road on to N Depaoli Road, traveled along the shoulder of N Depaoli and flowed off the shoulder into according to the site plans, an unnamed intermittent tributary to Millers Run. Conductivity readings were taken in the vegetation that is now impacted by sediment laden waters and they are as follows: 0.410 mS in the sediment laden puddle created from the flow going off the shoulder of the road, 0.464 mS in the vegetation adjacent to where the previous puddle reading was taken, 0.502 mS in some vegetation that is further in the intermittent tributary, and lastly 0.157 mS upslope of the Act 9 sign as a background reading. Though these readings subjugate that freshwater is being released, it is evident that sediment is still entering Waters of the Commonwealth. While onsite, the Department notified John Hulsey about the sediment entering the Waters of the Commonwealth and advised them to promptly cease all water release dust suppression activities on the access road.The Department recommends the Operator re-evaluate their dust suppression methods or implement measures to prevent sediment laden water from entering the intermittent unnamed tributary to Miller's Run.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the discharge of sediment into Waters of the Commonwealth.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/23/2025 to WILMOTH INTERESTS INC in Sheffield Township, Warren county. SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: WILMOTH INTERESTS INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/23/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 8253361
Permit API: 123-48915
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sheffield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/23/2025
Comments: A production equipment malfunction at the ANF 194 49 conventional well resulted in a release of crude oil and produced fluids. The Department was notified of the release by Jason Wells of Wilmoth Interests, Inc. The well was shut in from the gathering lines at the time of the malfunction. Therefore, when the malfunction occurred, downhole pressure released vertically from the well head causing crude oil to be sprayed a significant distance above the well before ultimately settling on the well pad and nearby vegetation. The approximate radius of crude oil laden vegetation and forest understory spans 200 feet in every direction from the well head. It appears that the heaviest aerial migration of the release traveled in a southeast to easterly direction from the well. The exact volume of the release is not immediately quantifiable, but it is clearly in excess of the one barrel limit set forth in the Department's spill policy.The bulk of the fluids released settled on the well pad. At the time of this inspection, 3-4 inches of crude oil and produced fluids were present on the pad near the well head. Recent rainfall contributed to the volume of liquid present on the pad, and some stormwater runoff was observed to be flowing down the access road berm and onto the pad. The specific conductance of standing fluid on the pad near the flow of stormwater was found to be 6,080 micro Siemens per centimeter. The specific conductance of standing fluid near the well head was found to be in excess of 20,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. No fluids with elevated specific conductance were observed beyond the well pad at the time of this inspection.The crude oil released on the well pad was observed to have migrated beyond the well pad and downslope in a southern direction. The brush barrier downslope of the well pad was heavily coated with crude oil. Pooled crude oil was observed to have migrated beyond the brush barrier on the forest floor and potentially via porous subsurface material. The extent of pooled crude oil visible on the surface of the forest floor was located at a point approximately 180 feet south/southeast of the well pad.Cleanup efforts began immediately after the release was discovered and brought under control. A ditch was excavated along the downslope end of the well pad to provide containment and a means by which to collect pooled fluids with a vac truck. Jason Wells contacted a consulting firm soon after the release with the intent to retain a consultant to oversee the cleanup process for Wilmoth. I spoke with Jason onsite at the time of this inspection to notify him that violations would be included with the inspection report.A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Comments: Site inspection by EPS Justin Abbott. Inspection conducted in response to spill notification submitted by EQT for the COP Tract 551-B pad. Inspection accompanied by EQT Lead EHS Coordinator Mark Barbier. Meeting on site with EQT Company Man Mike Hood. Weather conditions at time of inspection are partly cloudy, humid and 73 degrees F. Well stimulation activity is ceased at this time while EQT reviews SOPs.According to the Standard Detail Report, the spill notification was submitted by Mr. Barbier. At around 0800 hours, US Well Services was swabbing the well to switch over from the 6H to the 7H well. At that time, the open topped blender hopper overflowed releasing an estimated 140 barrels of fluid to containment, of which an unknown quantity of fluid overtopped the containment structures. During discussions on site with Mr. Barbier, the estimation was based on the fact that the pumps may have been releasing 20 barrels per minute for 7 minutes, although the exact volume can not be determined. The Department conducted conductivity screenings using an Oakton PCTS 50 meter and a Hanna Groline Soil Conductivity meter. Pooled fluid remaining within the containment structure was observed with conductivity readings between 7-8 mS/cm. Fluid within the north pad ditch and sumps outside of containment ranged from 3.92-5.37 mS/cm. Visual evidence of spilled fluid extended from a brushy area at the north conrer of the pad, along the entire ditch perimeter into the woods at the eastern corner of the pad where appeared to collect in a row of silt sock. Two vac trucks are present on site. One truck is vacuuming fluid from containment, a second truck is pumping spilled fluid collecting at he low point in the eastern corner of the pad ditch (photo 9). Visual observations near the blender unit indicated that fluid was released with sufficient force to release frac sand from the hopper. Two drums of frac sand were hand shoveled from the spill area (photo 10). Friction reducer material was also observed on pad rock outside containment. On the pad surface, spilled fluid is observed leaking through pad rock under the working tank secondary containment (photo 5). Pad rock affected by spilled fluid under containment is estimated to cover an area of 250 feet in length by 25-40 feet in width. The north ditch line channel is estimated at 400 feet in length with spilled fluid flowing an additional 25-50 feet off the north and east corners of the pad (photos 4 and 8). During discussions with Mr. Hood, when the well switch over occurs, down well fluid volumes are reduced and the blender valves must be adjusted to correspond to the reduced flow rate. Mr Hood indicated that the spill was caused by the blender operator falling asleep and failing to close a valve connecting the blender pumps to the working tanks during the well switch. Prior to site departure, Andy Steffee, Project Manager with Creston Environmental, arrived on site with a crew to begin conducting site characterization and sampling activity. Based on unknown volume of fluid spilled, Mr.Barbier indicated that EQT will immediately begin Act 2 remediation work. Well stimulation activity is expected to last into August at this location. Violations noted during this inspection and outstanding violations are extended.

Comments: Follow-up inspection conducted to review operator response to NOV associated with inspection report # 3373528. Weather conditions at time of inspection are sunny and 81 degrees F. During this inspection an Elk Environmental Services water truck is removing produced fluid from vertical tanks at northeast corner of pad. Areas across the well pad have been scraped and excavated to remove soils contaminated with regulated substances. An equipment operator with Fenton Transport is operating a skid-steer with loader bucket, an excavator and a mini-excavator to remove impacted soils. 22 steel bins are located on site along with 3 vacuum boxes for vacuuming up puddles following precipitation events. Areas of the pad that have been scraped or dug for removal include soils around well cellars and a large area of the eastern section of the pad toward the produced fluid tanks and where evaporator concentrated fluid secondary containment was located. Test pits and shallow trenches have been dug near the east and west sides of the well cellars. According to Mr. Maxwell, the limiting factor for the cleanup operation is the hauling and return of empty bins for contaminated soils. A Hanna Groline Soil Conductivity probe and organic free reagent water were used to screen for conductivity on the pad. Areas to the east and west of well cellars and between GPUs and produced fluid containment continue to show elevated conductivity (photos 3 and 5). These areas were pointed out to Mr Maxwell and Jackson and are expected to be scraped as disposal bins become available. Cleanup activity is expected to continue until soil screenings indicate conductivity levels under 1 mS/cm.There are no new violations at this time.

Comments: On 01/10/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Stech F69 well site following violations issued on 11/30/2023 (IR 3653747, Enforcement 422652). I was accompanied by WQS Supervisor, Sam Steingrabe (PADEP).Violations of 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a), 78.53, and 102.22(a)2ii were issued on 11/30/2023 due to the poor condition of the access road and lack of maintenance.The following was observed during inspection on 01/10/2023:Maintenance has not yet began on site. The lower section of the gravel access road pooling turbid water - this area is where crowing was previously recommended. I also recommended road to be pitched towards roadside channel to left. Water flowed/splashed from pooling towards stream valley and roadside channel, as seen by flattened grass. Culvert to right: outlet protection recommended; Chapter 105 permit may be required (Photos 1-4).Pooling of turbid water within potholes towards bend in road. Second, generally larger, area of pooling with turbid water in area around bend in road. Water seen flowing down access road to this area. Another culvert out letting into stream valley to the right of pooling (Photos 5-7).Upper section of gravel access road remained in a poor condition displaying channelization and accelerated erosion (Photos 8-13).On the paved section of the road, before the gravel access road, the failure on the slope past the guide rail was in a similar condition as previous inspection. This area may be prone to worsening condition (Photo 14). Another operator in the area agreed to maintaining this section of the road. This road is a private road that was abandoned by Fallowfield Township.Due to the maintenance on the gravel access road not commencing, the violations issued on 11/30/2023 remain outstanding. No additional violations are being issued at this time.
